parts.text: Which claim correctly settles that decision?

options.text: They are co-prime, because each product is greater than $1$.
They are not co-prime, because the prime $13$ appears in both factorisations.
They are co-prime, because $26$ and $39$ are the printed numbers in the stem.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that uses the prime factorisations.

stem: Imran has $26=2\times 13$ and $39=3\times 13$. He wants to decide whether $26$ and $39$ are co-prime from those prime factorisations.

part_answers.answer: Co-prime numbers share no common prime factor. Here 13 appears in both 26=2×13 and 39=3×13, so they are not co-prime.

teacher.key_rationale: A shared prime factor 13 means 26 and 39 are not co-prime. Looking only at product size or printed labels skips the common-prime test.
